Oral Judgment:

The appellant State of Maharashtra preferred present appeal against the impugned judgment and order of acquittal of respondent/accused rendered by the learned Magistrate in RCC No. 211 of 1993 for the ofence punishable under Section 7(i), 7(ii) read with Section 2(ia) (a), 2(ia)(b), 2(ia)(1)(ii) of State Of Maharashtra vs Prakash Rukman Kotalwar on 15 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43813926/
1 the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1962 and its rules framed therein (hereinafter referred to as the PFA Act).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to prosecution, the {2} CRAPL 388.97.odt complainant Shri Gopal Pathak was duly appointed as a Food Inspector at the relevant time in the year January 1993.
It has been alleged that on 27th January, 1999 at about 4.00 P.M., the complainant Shri Pathak paid visit to the Grocery Shop of the respondent/accused located in Gangakhed town.
The complainant Gopal Pathak disclosed his identity as Food Inspector to the respondent/accused and asked him to produce the licence of his shop but the respondent/accused did not produce the same.
The complainant Shri Gopal Pathak noticed that there was an item "Badi- saunf" seen kept for sale in the shop.
The complainant purchased 600 grams of item Badi-saunf after payment of Rs. 13.20 to the respondent.
Thereafter, he gave notice to the respondent in the Form No. VII of the PFA Act and communicated to him that the sample of item Badi-saunf was collected for the purpose of analysis.
Thereafter, he issued notice as prescribed under Section 14A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
The purchased item Badi-saunf was kept in the plain and clean paper which was divided in 3 equal parts and thereafter,item Badi-saunf was preserved in 3 clean and empty polythene packets.
These polythene packets were sealed and signed by him in the presence of panchas.
These samples were wrapped in the thick brown paper with lable on it.

After compliance of procedural formalities of seizure and sealing of the item Badi- saunf, the one sample was sent to the public analyst accompanied with the form No. VII with a request to carry out the analysis of the sample.
The one sample packet of Badi-saunf was given to the respondent.

Meanwhile, the complainant received information from the Licencing Authority that there was no licence granted in favour of respondent-shop owner to run the business of grocery shop for sale of food articles.

Thereafter,
report of the public analyst was also received from the Local Health Authority which revealed that the sample of item Badi-saunf sent to the public analyst for analysis contained extraneous non-permitted green colour matter. Therefore, {3} CRAPL 388.97.odt it did not conform to the standards as per the PFA Rules, 1955.
Thereafter, he sent the relevant papers to the Joint Commissioner Food and Drugs Administration to accord the prosecution sanction against respondent/accused.

After receipt of prosecution sanction (consent), the PW-1 Bhagwat Bobde, the successor of complainant Gopal Pathak, fled the complaint against respondent for the respective charges under the PFA Act and its rules, as indicated above.
2] In response to the summons, respondent accused appeared before the learned Magistrate and pleaded not guilty.
He denied the charges pitted against him.
In order to bring home guilt of the respondent/accused, prosecution examined both the Food Inspectors PW-1 Bhagwat Bobade and PW-2 Gopal Pathak to prove the charges against respondent/accused.
The prosecution also placed voluminous document on record including report of the public analyst (Exh.40).

After hearing both sides, and on appreciation of evidence adduced on record, the learned Magistrate arrived at the conclusion that the prosecution failed to prove the charges against respondent/accused beyond reasonable doubt.
There are legal infrmities in the report of the public analyst.
Therefore, it would unsafe to fasten the guilt on the respondent/accused.

In the result, learned Magistrate exonerated respondent/accused for the charges pitted against him and rendered the impugned judgment and order of acquittal of the respondent which is the subject matter of present appeal.

3] Learned APP appearing for the appellant State of Maharashtra vehemently submits that the learned trial court did not appreciate the evidence on record in its proper perspective and State Of Maharashtra vs Prakash Rukman Kotalwar on 15 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43813926/
2 committed error in acquittal of respondent accused in this court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned APP submits that there was due compliance of Rule 7(3) of {4} CRAPL 388.97.odt the PFA Act and, therefore, it would fallacious to discard the report of the public analyst.
In the report of public analyst the date of analysis of item Badi-saunf was not shown but it would not fatal to the prosecution case.
According to learned APP, it is not necessary for the complainant to prove that the food article seized was not ft for human consumption.

He submits that sanctioning authority i.e. Joint Commissioner Food and Drugs Administration has considered the entire aspects of the crime and thereafter, accorded prosecution sanction (consent Exh.51).
Therefore, the conclusion drawn by the learned Magistrate was erroneous, illegal and deserves to be set aside and quashed.
The respondent/accused is to be convicted for the charges pitted against him.

The learned APP drawn attention to the evidence of PW-2 Food Inspector Gopal Pathak who has scrupulously followed the procedure prescribed under law for seizure and sealing of the articles and sending it to the authority of public analyst for analysis.

4] The learned counsel for respondent/accused assailed that the learned Magistrate has correctly appreciated the circumstances on record and drawn inference that respondent./accused could not be held guilty for the charges pitted against him on the basis of evidence adduced on record on behalf of prosecution.
The learned counsel for respondent/accused submits that in the report of public analyst (Exh.40), the date of actual analysis of the item Badi-saunf was not mentioned.
The item was sent to the public analyst on 2.2.1993 whereas, its report of analyais received to the complainant on 4.3.1993.
According to learned counsel for respondent/accused it was imperative for the public analyst to mention the date on which the actual analysis of sample was taken place.
There is legal lacuna in the present case.

He relied upon the ratio laid down in the case of " State of Maharashtra Vs. Tirath Singha Saudagar Singh Khanuja" (1986) 1 FCA 166.
{5} CRAPL 388.97.odt

entities.text: State of Maharashtra Vs. Tirath Singha Saudagar Singh Khanuja" (1986) 1 FCA 166
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel further raised objection that in the report of public analyst it was shown that sample was insect infested but it has not mentioned whether it was unft for human consumption.
Moreover, the report does not make it clear that whether the extraneous non permitted colour detected from the sample was dangerous and hazardous for human consumption.
The learned counsel contends that the entire prosecution case rests on the public analyst's report which is not in conformity with the provisions of law.
Therefore, inference drawn by the learned trial court is just, proper and reasonable one.
It does not warrant any interference.

5] Having given anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on behalf of both sides, as well as to the voluminous documentary evidence produced on record on behalf of prosecution, I fnd that the arguments advance on behalf of respondent/accused more formidable and sustainable one.

Admittedly, learned trial court proceeded to acquit the respondent/accused on the ground that (1)
public analyst did not mention date of analysis of sample in the report (Exh.40) and there may be delay in actual analysis of the samples.
(2) report of public analyst (Exh.40) did not made it clear that the samples of item Badi-saunf was unft for human consumption.

The respondent/accused also raised the objection in regard to the mode and manner in which the prosecution sanction/consent letter (Exh.51) was issued by the Joint Commissioner Food and Drugs Administration Department in this case.

sentences.text: He took over the charge from his {6} CRAPL 388.97.odt predecessor PW-2 Gopal Pathak on 9.6.1993.
He deposed about the fling of criminal complaint before the learned Magistrate Gangakhed bearing RCC No. 211 of 1993.
PW-2 Gopal Pathak deposed that on 27.1.1993, he was attached to the Food and Drugs Department Parbhani as Food Inspector.
He visited to the grocery shop of respondent/accused on 27.1.1993 and collected the sample of item Badi-saunf from his shop.
He complied with the procedural formalities of collection of item, its seizure and sealing for analysis by the Public Analyst.
The respondent/accused did not put into controversy the factual aspects of collection of sample and its sealing etc. as well as sending it to the public analyst as per the provisions of law.
However, the respondent/accused assailed the genuineness of the report of public analyst (Exh.40) in this case.
It was admitted fact that samples were received to the public analyst on 2.2.1993.
Thereafter, the complainant received the report of public analyst dated 4.3.1993.

After perusal of the report (Exh.40) issued by the Public Analyst it appears that there was no reference about the date on which the samples were actually taken for analysis by the concerned authority.

The learned Single Judge of this court Bench at Nagpur, in the case of "Tirath Singh" cited supra observed in para. 8 as under :-
"Exh.31 is the report of Public Analyst, Public Health Laboratory, Nagpur dated 3.9.1980.
The report is conspicuously silent about the date of analysis.
This is an important lacuna in the report, which vitiates the entire prosecution.
The Bombay High Court in Shaikh Hamid Vs. Dagu and another, 1979 (I) FAC 334, refused to interefere with acquittal in view of the absence of the date on the report of Analysit.

entities.text: Shaikh Hamid Vs. Dagu and another, 1979 (I) FAC 334
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was observed, "the crucial factor against prosecution, however, is the lacuna in the report Exh.23 of the Public Analyust.

Looking at the report, it is clear that it does not,
at any place, indicate the date of the analysis nor does it give any indication of the time of the analysis.

Though time may not be very relevant factor,date certainly is ...
...

In the absence of any date of analysis of the sample in the report of the Public Analyst, the sample could as well have been analysed on the date of the report which is 3rd October, 1975 or perhaps a day or two earlier.
Analysis of the {7} CRAPL 388.97.odt sample several days after its receipt can not be safely ruled out.

It is,
therefore, difcult and unsafe to base a conviction.
Inter alia, placing reliance on such a report which contains a very important lacuna as aforesaid."

In the instant case, the sample was taken on 22.7.1980 and the same was sent to Public Analyst on 23.7.80,
which was received by him on 25.7.80.
The report fo the Pubilc Analyst is dated 3.9.80.
From the above, it is clear the sample was analysed after about 38 days after it was received by the Public Analyst.
The credibility of the report, therefore, becomes highly in question.".
7] In the matter in hand also, sample of Badi-saunf was collected on 27.1.1993.
Thereafter, it was forwarded to the ofce of Public Analyst Pune which was received to it on 2.2.1993.
The report of the Public Analyst (Exh.40) was received to the concerned Department for further process.
The report of Public Analyst dated 4.3.1993, as referred above, does not make it clear as to on which date the samples of Badi-saunf were actually taken for analysis.
Moreover, the report also shows that sample was having insect damage matter to the extent 0.24%.

The Public Analyst arrived at the conclusion State Of Maharashtra vs Prakash Rukman Kotalwar on 15 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43813926/
4

sentences.text: that there was extraneous non permitted green colour detected in the sample and it did not conform to the standards of "Saunf" as per the PFA Rules, 1955.
8] Admittedly, the report of Public Analyst (Exh.40) does not indicate as to exactly on which date the sample was taken for analysis.
The possibility of delay in analysis of item Badi-saunf by Public Analyst cannot be ruled out and such delay would adversely afect genuineness of result of its analysis.

Moreover, the report is silent as to whether the samples were unft for human consumption,
as well as the extraneous non-permitted green colour detected in the sample would be the criteria sufcient to conclude that it was an "adulterous sample" as defned under Section 2 of the PFA Act.
In such circumstances, I am of the considered opinion that the fnding of learned Magistrate resulted into acquittal of respondent/accused appears to be just, proper and reasonable one.
The entire edifce of {8} CRAPL 388.97.odt the prosecution case rests on the genuineness of Public Analyst's report (Exh.40).
But, there are legal infrmities in the report as mentioned above.
The report appears incredulous, dubious and does not inspire confdence.
In such circumstances, it would unsafe to fasten guilt on the respondent/accused on the basis of such suspicious and doubtful report of Public Analyst (Exh.40).
Therefore, there is no propriety to cause any interference in the fnding expressed by the learned Magistrate for acquittal of respondent/accused.
In the result, the appeal preferred on behalf of prosecution being devoid of merit, deserves to be dismissed.
Same is accordingly dismissed.
No orders as to costs.
[K.K. SONAWANE] JUDGE.
Grt/-.
